ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the correct reply to shukran (thank you)? (1 mark)
   A. ismii
   B. marhaban
   C. maʿa s-salaama
   D. ʿafwan

2. Which Kiswahili word comes from the Arabic word kitaab? (1 mark)
   A. mti
   B. maji
   C. nyumba
   D. kitabu

3. Which Arabic word means "I am well"? (1 mark)
   A. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ
   B. اسْمِي
   C. مَرْحَبًا
   D. أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ

4. How is the Arabic word أُسْرَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. bint
   B. ukht
   C. usra
   D. khaal

5. Which Arabic sentence means "This is my father." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا أَبِي
   B. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   C. أَبِي يَعْمَلُ
   D. هَذِهِ أُمِّي

6. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا عِنْدَ الْبَابِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The cat is under the bed.
   B. The lamp is above the table.
   C. I am at the door.
   D. The book is on the table.

7. What does the Arabic word الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) mean? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. Sunday
   C. Tuesday
   D. day

8. How is the Arabic word غَدًا read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ghadan
   B. madrasa
   C. yawm
   D. usbuuʿ

9. What is an inferential question? (1 mark)
   A. A question with no answer
   B. A question whose answer is not stated but can be worked out from clues
   C. A question whose answer is stated in the text
   D. A question about spelling

10. What does the Arabic sentence أَشْرَبُ الْحَلِيبَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I eat bread.
   B. I drink milk.
   C. I like bananas.
   D. I drink water.

11. Which Arabic sentence means "I eat bread." (1 mark)
   A. أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ
   B. أُحِبُّ الْعَصِيرَ
   C. آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ
   D. أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ

12. Which Arabic word means "open the door"? (1 mark)
   A. أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ
   B. اُخْرُجْ
   C. افْتَحِ الْبَابَ
   D. قِفْ

13. How is the Arabic word أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. uktub
   B. aghmiD ʿaynayka
   C. ismaʿ
   D. ilmis anfaka

14. What does the Arabic word جِسْمٌ (jism) mean? (1 mark)
   A. neck
   B. back
   C. leg
   D. body

15. What does the Arabic word شَمْسٌ (shams) mean? (1 mark)
   A. sunny
   B. sun
   C. weather
   D. flower

16. In a short speech, what does the sentence anaa fii S-Saffi r-raabiʿ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am a teacher
   B. I am in the kitchen
   C. I am in Grade 4
   D. I am at the door

17. Which sound does the Arabic letter ش make? (1 mark)
   A. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch
   B. sh as in shop
   C. t as in tap
   D. k as in kite

18. How do you read the syllable تَ? (1 mark)
   A. buu
   B. ta
   C. nu
   D. tu

19. Which sound does the Arabic letter م make? (1 mark)
   A. m as in mat
   B. d as in dog
   C. l as in lamp
   D. t as in tap

20. Which day is al-khamiis? (1 mark)
   A. Tuesday
   B. Friday
   C. Thursday
   D. Saturday

21. What does the Arabic sentence هَدِيَّةٌ لِأَمِينَةَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. A gift for Amina.
   B. Above the table there is a balloon.
   C. This is a party.
   D. On the table there is a cake.

22. What does the Arabic question mark ؟ tell the reader? (1 mark)
   A. Stop reading
   B. The voice falls
   C. Read very fast
   D. The voice rises at the end

23. How is the Arabic word سُكَّرٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. sukkar
   B. burtuqaal
   C. jazar
   D. lahm

24. How is the Arabic word كَتِفٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. shaʿr
   B. katif
   C. sinn
   D. raʾs

25. What does the Arabic sentence الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is in the sky.
   B. In the room there is a bed.
   C. How beautiful the environment is!
   D. And the rain is from the sky.

26. Why should a knife be kept out of the reach of small children? (1 mark)
   A. It is expensive
   B. It is old
   C. It can cause harm
   D. It is heavy

27. Which Arabic word means "book"? (1 mark)
   A. حَقِيبَةٌ
   B. سِكِّينٌ
   C. سَاعَةٌ
   D. كِتَابٌ

28. What is the difference between ف (faa) and ق (qaaf)? (1 mark)
   A. faa has two dots above and qaaf has one
   B. faa has one dot above and qaaf has two dots above
   C. faa has a dot below
   D. They have no dots

29. How many forms can an Arabic letter have at most? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Four: alone, start, middle and end
   C. One
   D. Two

30. What sits on the baseline in Arabic writing? (1 mark)
   A. Only the vowels
   B. Most of the letters
   C. Only the dots
   D. Nothing

31. What does the Arabic word أَخٌ (akh) mean? (1 mark)
   A. mother's brother
   B. father's sister
   C. son
   D. brother

32. Which Arabic word means "clock"? (1 mark)
   A. غُرْفَةٌ
   B. مِصْبَاحٌ
   C. سَاعَةٌ
   D. كُرْسِيٌّ

33. How is the Arabic word لَذِيذٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. taawila
   B. baarid
   C. ladhiidh
   D. as-salaamu ʿalaykum

34. What does the Arabic sentence أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. We dance.
   B. I have a gift.
   C. My mother cooks the food.
   D. I like the party.

35. What is word spacing? (1 mark)
   A. The number of dots
   B. The height of letters
   C. The small space between words
   D. The colour of ink

36. Which Arabic word means "fruit"? (1 mark)
   A. لَذِيذٌ
   B. إِصْبَعٌ
   C. فَاكِهَةٌ
   D. يَوْمٌ

37. Which Arabic word means "milk"? (1 mark)
   A. مَاءٌ
   B. حَلِيبٌ
   C. جَزَرٌ
   D. مَوْزٌ

38. Which Arabic word means "neck"? (1 mark)
   A. بَطْنٌ
   B. جِسْمٌ
   C. سِنٌّ
   D. رَقَبَةٌ

39. What does the Arabic word شَعْرٌ (shaʿr) mean? (1 mark)
   A. finger
   B. heart
   C. mouth
   D. hair

40. Which Arabic word means "sunny"? (1 mark)
   A. حَارٌّ
   B. شَمْسٌ
   C. مُشْمِسٌ
   D. غَائِمٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name two common foods in your area and write one Arabic sentence about one of them, with its meaning. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Write five things or rooms found in a home in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

43. Translate into English: al-kursiyyu ʿinda l-baab (2 marks)

44. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'I eat bread and I drink milk.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

45. Give two reasons why reading is important. (2 marks) (2 marks)

46. Write three Arabic questions about a picture of a party and give their meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

47. Write the Arabic sounds and meanings of four position words. (4 marks) (4 marks)

48. Translate into English: aghsilu wajhii (2 marks)

49. Write the seven days in Arabic sounds and say what the first five names come from. (5 marks) (5 marks)

50. Translate into English: al-qittatu taHta s-sariir (2 marks)

51. Translate into English: al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba (2 marks)

52. Translate into English: haadhaa jismii (2 marks)

53. Translate into English: ashrabu sh-shaaya (2 marks)

54. Translate into English: al-jawwu haarr (2 marks)

55. Say what the words abii yaʿmalu and ummii tatbukhu mean, and name one thing each parent does. (4 marks) (4 marks)

56. Translate into English: aakulu l-khubza (2 marks)

57. Translate into English: lii yadaani (2 marks)

58. Translate into English: haadhihi hafla (2 marks)

59. Describe the steps for learning to write a new letter. (4 marks) (4 marks)

60. Translate into English: at-taawilatu Sagiira (2 marks)

61. Give three checks you should do after writing a sentence in Arabic. (3 marks) (3 marks)

62. Describe how to make a vocabulary bank of words about the home. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — ʿafwan
   ʿafwan means 'you are welcome' and is the polite reply to thanks.

2. D — kitabu
   The Kiswahili word kitabu (book) came from Arabic kitaab. The other words are Bantu words.

3. D — أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ
   أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ (anaa bi-khayr) means I am well.

4. C — usra
   أُسْرَةٌ is read usra and means family.

5. A — هَذَا أَبِي
   هَذَا أَبِي (haadhaa abii) means: This is my father.

6. C — I am at the door.
   أَنَا عِنْدَ الْبَابِ (anaa ʿinda l-baab) means: I am at the door.

7. B — Sunday
   الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) means Sunday.

8. A — ghadan
   غَدًا is read ghadan and means tomorrow.

9. B — A question whose answer is not stated but can be worked out from clues
   For inferential questions you use clues in the text to work out the answer.

10. B — I drink milk.
   أَشْرَبُ الْحَلِيبَ (ashrabu l-haliiba) means: I drink milk.

11. C — آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ
   آكُلُ الْخُبْزَ (aakulu l-khubza) means: I eat bread.

12. C — افْتَحِ الْبَابَ
   افْتَحِ الْبَابَ (iftahi l-baab) means open the door.

13. B — aghmiD ʿaynayka
   أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ is read aghmiD ʿaynayka and means close your eyes.

14. D — body
   جِسْمٌ (jism) means body.

15. B — sun
   شَمْسٌ (shams) means sun.

16. C — I am in Grade 4
   Saff means class and raabiʿ means fourth.

17. B — sh as in shop
   The letter ش makes the sound sh as in shop.

18. B — ta
   تَ is read ta.

19. A — m as in mat
   The letter م makes the sound m as in mat.

20. C — Thursday
   al-khamiis is Thursday, the fifth day, from the word for five.

21. A — A gift for Amina.
   هَدِيَّةٌ لِأَمِينَةَ (hadiyya li-Aminata) means: A gift for Amina.

22. D — The voice rises at the end
   A question ends with a rising voice.

23. A — sukkar
   سُكَّرٌ is read sukkar and means sugar.

24. B — katif
   كَتِفٌ is read katif and means shoulder.

25. A — The sun is in the sky.
   الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ (ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i) means: The sun is in the sky.

26. C — It can cause harm
   Sharp items can hurt small children.

27. D — كِتَابٌ
   كِتَابٌ (kitaab) means book.

28. B — faa has one dot above and qaaf has two dots above
   Only the dots separate these two letters.

29. B — Four: alone, start, middle and end
   A joining letter can look different alone, at the start, in the middle and at the end of a word.

30. B — Most of the letters
   Most letters rest on the baseline. Alif stands tall above it.

31. D — brother
   أَخٌ (akh) means brother.

32. C — سَاعَةٌ
   سَاعَةٌ (saaʿa) means clock.

33. C — ladhiidh
   لَذِيذٌ is read ladhiidh and means delicious.

34. C — My mother cooks the food.
   أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ (ummii tatbukhu T-taʿaam) means: My mother cooks the food.

35. C — The small space between words
   Word spacing is the neat gap between one word and the next.

36. C — فَاكِهَةٌ
   فَاكِهَةٌ (faakiha) means fruit.

37. B — حَلِيبٌ
   حَلِيبٌ (haliib) means milk.

38. D — رَقَبَةٌ
   رَقَبَةٌ (raqaba) means neck.

39. D — hair
   شَعْرٌ (shaʿr) means hair.

40. C — مُشْمِسٌ
   مُشْمِسٌ (mushmis) means sunny.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example maize and bananas. al-mawzu ladhiidh. The banana is delicious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two foods, 1 mark for a correct sentence and 1 mark for its meaning.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example bayt (house), ghurfa (room), matbakh (kitchen), hammaam (bathroom), hadiiqa (garden).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The chair is at the door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: aakulu l-khubza wa ashrabu l-haliiba. I eat bread and I drink milk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to learn new words and information, and it gives us enjoyment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example ayna l-kaʿka? (Where is the cake?) man haadhaa? (Who is this?) maadhaa fawqa t-taawila? (What is above the table?)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question with meaning.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: fii (in), ʿalaa (on), taHta (under), fawqa (above).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: I wash my face.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: al-ahad, al-ithnayn, ath-thulaathaa', al-arbiʿaa', al-khamiis, al-jumuʿa, as-sabt. The first five come from the numbers one to five.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for the days (2 for five or six, 1 for three or four) and 2 marks for the numbers clue.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: The cat is under the bed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: The pen is in the bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: I drink tea.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: abii yaʿmalu: My father works. ummii tatbukhu: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each translation and 1 mark for each role named.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: I eat bread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have two hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is a party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Trace the model; copy it several times from right to left; write it from memory and compare; add and check the dots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: The table is small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: Did I write from right to left? Are the letters neat and joined? Are the dots and marks in place? Does the sentence make sense?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid check.

62. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each Arabic word on a card with a picture; write the sound and meaning on the back; keep the cards in a box or on a chart and use them to practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.
